newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemeni president names new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Yemeni president names new prime minister.

text.p: Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh on Wednesday named Faraj Said Bin Ghanem, a Polish-educated economist, as prime minister, state-run television said.

It said Saleh issued a decree asking Bin Ghanem, a former planning minister, to form a new government after Yemen's general elections last month in which the ruling General People's Party (GPC) won a majority in parliament.

Bin Ghanem replaces Abdul-Aziz Abdul-Ghani who on Monday presented the government's resignation to Saleh following the April 27 polls, the first general elections since a 1994 civil war in the impoverished Arab state.
Officials said Bin Ghanem, an independent and currently Yemen's ambassador to the European headquarters of the United Nations in Geneva, would form the government "soon".
"The cabinet is expected to include many new faces of mostly technocrats," one official said.
Diplomats said Saleh's choice reflected his commitment to push ahead with tough economic reforms agreed with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
